title: The Resilience of the Iceberg Rose
content: The Iceberg climbing rose is one of the most popular and vigorous climbing roses available. It produces abundant clusters of pure white, double flowers that bloom continuously from early spring right through to late autumn. It is incredibly disease-resistant and requires very little maintenance, making it perfect for beginners.

title: Caring for the Mister Lincoln
content: Mister Lincoln is legendary for its deep, velvety red petals and an intoxicating, classic damask fragrance. To get the best blooms, ensure it receives at least 6 hours of direct sunlight and keep the soil consistently moist but not waterlogged. Regular pruning in late winter is essential for vigorous spring growth.

title: Golden Showers: A Bright Addition
content: If you are looking to brighten up a dull wall or trellis, the Golden Showers climbing rose is exceptional. Its loosely double, daffodil-yellow blooms open beautifully. Unlike many climbers, it can tolerate dappled shade. I recommend tying the canes horizontally to encourage more lateral blooming shoots.

title: Don Juan: The Dark Red Climber
content: For a striking contrast against a white fence, nothing beats the Don Juan. The dark velvety red blooms are huge, and the fragrance is intensely sweet. It prefers warmer climates and handles the southern heat much better than other red climbers.

title: Tropicana: A Burst of Coral
content: The Tropicana rose brings a tropical vibe right to the garden. The vivid coral-orange color stands out against the dark glossy foliage. It is highly susceptible to mildew though, so make sure you give it plenty of air circulation.

title: The Classic Double Delight
content: The Double Delight is an absolute masterpiece. The creamy white center bleeds into a vibrant strawberry red edge. The amount of red depends on how much UV light the petals receive. Its spicy, classic scent is unforgettable.
